title: Extract spoken page numbers from a recording
instructions: Create a workflow that transcribes a supplied audio recording and reports the page numbers named in it.

workflow_input.question:
Hi, I was out sick from my classes on Friday, so I'm trying to figure out what I need to study for my Calculus mid-term next week. My friend from class sent me an audio recording of Professor Willowbrook giving out the recommended reading for the test, but my headphones are broken :(

Could you please listen to the recording for me and tell me the page numbers I'm supposed to go over? I've attached a file called Homework.mp3 that has the recording. Please provide just the page numbers as a comma-delimited list. And please provide the list in ascending order.

criteria.title: Transcribes or interprets the retrieved audio
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow submits the retrieved audio itself to a step capable of turning speech into text or otherwise interpreting audio content — a speech-to-text service, an audio-capable model, or an equivalent skill step — so that the answer derives from what is spoken in the recording. PASS: the audio bytes (or a reference such a service can resolve) are passed into such a step. FAIL: the workflow only handles the recording's address as text, or answers from the question's wording alone without the audio ever reaching an interpreting step.

criteria.title: The audio recording is retrieved with an authenticated request
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow retrieves the audio recording from the address supplied in `audio_url` using a request that carries an Authorization header, because the host serving it refuses unauthenticated requests. PASS: a step fetches the `audio_url` value and attaches an Authorization header whose value is a %%[A-Z0-9_]+%%-form secret reference. This criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used, nor which step type performs the fetch. FAIL: the fetch carries no Authorization header at all, or the workflow never retrieves the resource and instead reasons about the address alone.

criteria.title: Workflow accepts a caller-supplied input named exactly `audio_url`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `audio_url`, and fetches the audio recording from that value rather than from a hard-coded address. PASS if the produced workflow JSON references an input/variable named `audio_url` and uses it as the location of the audio recording it retrieves. FAIL if the audio recording's address is embedded as a fixed literal, or the input is declared under any other name — a rerun supplies the value under the name `audio_url` and cannot drive a workflow that reads a different name.

criteria.title: Workflow accepts a caller-supplied input named exactly `question`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `question`, and the artifact's behavior is driven by that input's value rather than a literal. This is assessed at the artifact level: PASS if the produced workflow JSON references an input/variable named `question` and uses it to build the request. FAIL if the workflow embeds the question text directly with no `question` input reference, or declares the input under any other name (e.g. `query`, `prompt`, `userQuestion`) — a rerun supplies the value under the name `question` and cannot drive a workflow that reads a different name.

criteria.title: Authorization headers contain no plaintext credential
criteria.match_criteria: On every step that makes an outbound call, the Authorization header value must not embed live credential material of any kind. PASS: the Authorization value is a secret reference in the authoring form %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% — optionally Bearer-wrapped, provided the wrapped token is itself a %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%%-form reference rather than a literal string. Any well-formed %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% name passes; this criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used. FAIL: an Authorization header contains a plaintext API key (for example a literal beginning sk-) or a raw key embedded directly in the URL query string or path.

criteria.title: Secret references use the required authoring form
criteria.match_criteria: Every secret reference in the produced workflow must use the required authoring form %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% — uppercase letters, digits and underscores between paired %% markers — and never the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}. The authoring form %%…%% and the runtime form {{ … }} are two spellings of the same secret-substitution mechanism; %%…%% is required in authored workflow JSON. This criterion asserts only the SHAPE of the reference: it never asserts WHICH secret name is used, and an unresolved %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% is a warning upstream, never a failure here. FAIL: any malformed reference — a lowercase or hyphenated name such as %%my-secret-name%%, surrounding spaces such as %% NAME %%, or a single-percent variant such as %NAME% — or the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}, including defaulted variants such as {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME | default: '' }}.

criteria.title: Workflow is structurally valid
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow JSON satisfies all three structural requirements: (1) there is at least one connection whose source is "start" (or the workflow has a designated start node/step); (2) every step is reachable via an unbroken chain of connections from start (no orphaned steps); (3) there is at least one edge whose target is "system.succeed" (or the equivalent terminal node), ensuring the workflow can reach a successful completion state. A workflow missing any one of these three is structurally invalid and fails this criterion.

criteria.title: The run output is a direct answer, not scaffolding
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow — not against the workflow JSON. PASS: the output is a direct answer to the question asked — the bare value or a short sentence containing it; casing and surrounding phrasing are not asserted. FAIL: the output is empty, an error message or stack-trace payload, raw request/response scaffolding with no answer extracted, a verbatim echo of the question, a refusal, or a statement that the answer could not be determined.

criteria.title: The run output states the correct answer
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow — not against the workflow JSON. The reference answer is supplied to the judge alongside this task; it is deliberately not restated here, so that the corpus index shipped to the browser carries no answer key. PASS: the answer conveyed by the output matches that reference answer. Exact formatting is not asserted: a short sentence containing the correct value passes, as do differences in casing, surrounding punctuation, or an equivalent spelling of the same value. A numeric answer must match the reference number exactly; a list answer must contain the same items; a named answer must name the same entity. FAIL: the output states a different value, hedges between several candidate values without committing to the correct one, or names no answer at all.
